newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine gov't to appeal telecom ruling - Telam.
newsitem.headline: Argentine gov't to appeal telecom ruling - Telam.

text.p: The Argentine government will appeal a federal judge's ruling Friday which suspended a decree authorizing telephone companies to restructure their rates, state news agency Telam quoted a source as saying.
The source in the Communications Secretariat told Telam that the government move will, at least temporarily, suspend the judge's ruling and leave the new rate structure intact.
No Communications Secretariat spokesman was immediately available to comment on the report.
Judge Maria Jose Sarmiento earlier Friday suspended last week's new rate structure pending a ruling on a court case to have the tariff changes reversed. The nation's Ombudsman brought the case.
Shares in Telefonica de Argentina and Telecom de Argentina surged last week after the decree authorizing the rate changes.

Telefonica and Telecom had waged a long lobbying compaign for the tariff changes, which they said would make charges fairer for business in the provinces. They also hoped it would make them more competitive when the Argentine phone market is thrown open to all competitors, probably in the year 2000.
They also face competition from offshore call-back services offering cheap long-distance calls.

But consumer groups and opposition parties fought hard against the changes, and argued in public hearings ending in December 1996 that private users' telephone bills would rise and the phone companies would pocket the difference.
The companies argued the restructuring would not mean extra profits.
